newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed higher on Friday, lifted out of a mostly flat session by the 1230 GMT release of U.S. producer price index data, which soothed near term inflation worries and boosted Wall Street and bond markets.

"That's basically it. We were going nowhere all day and then the PPI figure came in and pushed the market up," said one dealer. "People were a bit worried about inflation but the PPI was around consensus and that was enough to push the market."
The AEX share index closed 2.83 points higher at 587.20, back from a day's high of 588.19, having traded in a narrow range around Friday's close for much of the session.

The U.S. Labor Department reported overall PPI rose 0.2 percent in September, in line with consensus forecasts. "There was a bit of worry that the figures might be above forecasts so today shows a bit of relief in the market," said a dealer.
Dutch shares had drifted all morning, drawing little support from a steady dollar, inclined to meander ahead of the PPI data.

Dealers said they would be watching to see how Wall Street digested the PPI data before attempting to predict Monday's mood on the AEX. "Wall Street's doing pretty well at our close but we'd have to wait and see whether people will try to push the market back up to the (590.76 all-time) high," said a trader.
Philips rose 80 cents to 64.80, drawing fresh support from U.S. book to bill data earlier this week showing a stronger than expected rise in orders for semi-conductors.

Music and movies firm PolyGram closed 90 cents higher at 89.20 guilders, reversing an earlier 1.00 guilder fall triggered by an article in the Financial Times newspaper saying the international music industry was slowing down after years of strong growth.
The newspaper said a prolonged slowdown could have serious implications for a number of firms including PolyGram. Dealers said the shares later joined the overall market rally.

Dutch PTT was up 0.80 guilders to 61.00, boosted by a perception that it has underperformed the market recently and on optimism that its planned acquisition of Australian transport firm TNT will enhance earnings.
Other blue chips showed Royal Dutch 1.70 guilders higher at 277.80 and Unilever 60 cents firmer at 269.20 guilders. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
